title: Council opposes Bill 23 and ends councillor benefits
subtitle: Airport runway design, transit funding, microloans, child care fees, affordable housing and a new HR system.
overview: Regional Council adopted committee reports that asked the Province to reconsider Bill 23 and extend consultation. The resolution warns the bill could weaken regional land-use planning, groundwater protection and development charge funding for infrastructure. It also asks for lasting federal and provincial infrastructure funding. The same package rescinded the post-service benefits for councillors approved in November and ended extended benefits for past councillors on December 31, 2022. A citizen advisory committee will later study councillor pay and benefits.

Council also approved a one-time microloan program for small businesses, a design choice for Bleams Road improvements, a reduction in home child care parent fees from January 1, 2023, and priority affordable housing projects. It approved more money for the airport runway extension design {{vote:m4}} and transit projects for federal funding {{vote:m5}}.

After a closed session, council awarded a contract to PricewaterhouseCoopers for a shared human resources information system with Waterloo Regional Police {{vote:m10}}. The Region's share is estimated at $6.4M.

decisions.detail: Council asked the Province to reconsider Bill 23, extend consultation, explain its effect on housing affordability, and fund growth infrastructure, with the resolution sent to provincial and municipal bodies.

Council rescinded the November decision on post-service benefits, ended extended benefits for past councillors on December 31, 2022, and directed staff to draft terms for a citizen committee reviewing remuneration.
Council awarded PricewaterhouseCoopers a contract, estimated at $6.4M for the Region's share, for a joint system with Waterloo Regional Police {{vote:m10}}.
Council increased the MTE Consultants design contract by $166,450 and raised the 2022 airport capital budget by $169,400 {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the projects to submit under the final Investing in Canada Infrastructure Program public transit intake and authorized the agreements {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved up to $250,000 for a small business microloan program and the recommended design for Bleams Road improvements.

decisions.item: Child care fees and affordable housing
decisions.detail: Council cut home child care parent fees for children under six by 52.75% from January 1, 2023 and approved priority affordable housing projects with development charge grants.

debate: On the human resources system, one councillor asked for a public staff presentation because it was the first public discussion of a significant project.
Staff said the Region relies on manual processes and spreadsheets, and some systems are near the end of support. They said this adds risk and cost and hurts recruiting.

Staff said the item came before the February budget because the selected proposal expires on December 20. They ranked it near the top of technology priorities, and a councillor asked whether it was the top priority.

On transit funding, one councillor said the federal government is designing a successor to the current program and said a green focus is likely. The councillor suggested municipalities press for better public recognition of funding announcements.
A delegate from a museum fundraising group described donations for costuming and audio equipment. Councillors thanked the group.
